Japan’s Industrial Intermediate Prod Sector Posts Modest Growth in Q1

TOKYO, April 25—Japan’s industrial intermediate products sector saw modest growth in the first quarter of the year, buoyed by steady domestic demand and recovering export orders, according to data released Thursday by the Japan Industrial Materials Federation.

The federation reported that total shipments for the January-March period rose 2.4% from a year earlier, reaching 1.89 trillion yen ($12.6 billion). Output increased 2.1% year-on-year, extending a gradual recovery that began in late 2023.

“We are seeing continued resilience in the automotive and electronics supply chains, with increased orders for specialty steels and advanced polymers,” said Akira Naito, federation spokesperson. “While global uncertainties persist, Japanese manufacturers are capitalizing on stable demand in Asia and North America.”

Mitsuba Chemical Industries, a key sector player, reported a 3.7% rise in quarterly operating profit, citing stronger shipments of resins and industrial adhesives. “We expect a steady performance throughout 2024 as infrastructure and technology investments drive demand,” said company president Emi Fujimoto.

However, some analysts noted that cost pressures remain. “Input prices, especially for energy and imported chemicals, are still elevated, which may weigh on margins,” said Tomoko Saito, senior economist at Hoshida Research.

The Japan Industrial Workers’ Union welcomed the positive figures but urged vigilance. “Sustainable growth will depend on continued investment in innovation and skills,” said union leader Keiji Yamamoto.

Industry officials expect output to remain stable in the coming months, supported by ongoing capital expenditure and gradual recovery in overseas markets.
